gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void record_dead_and_set_regs_1 (rtx dest, const_rtx setter, void *data)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void record_promoted_value (rtx_insn *insn, rtx subreg)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static bool reg_truncated_to_mode (machine_mode mode, const_rtx x)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Check if X, a register, is known to contain a value already truncated to MODE. In this case we can use a subreg to refer to the truncated value even though in the generic case we would need an explicit truncation.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static bool record_truncated_value (rtx x)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: If X is a hard reg or a subreg record the mode that the register is accessed in. For non-TARGET_TRULY_NOOP_TRUNCATION targets we might be able to turn a truncate into a subreg using this information. Return true if traversing X is complete.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void record_truncated_values (rtx *loc, void *data ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static rtx get_last_value (const_rtx x)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void reg_dead_at_p_1 (rtx dest, const_rtx x, void *data ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static bool reg_dead_at_p (rtx reg, rtx_insn *insn)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Return true if REG is known to be dead at INSN. We scan backwards from INSN. If we hit a REG_DEAD note or a CLOBBER referencing REG, it is dead. gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void mark_used_regs_combine (rtx x)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Note hard registers in X that are used.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: rtx remove_death (unsigned int regno, rtx_insn *insn)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Remove register number REGNO from the dead registers list of INSN. Return the note used to record the death, if there was one.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void move_deaths (rtx x, rtx maybe_kill_insn, int from_luid, rtx_insn *to_insn, rtx *pnotes)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: For each register (hardware or pseudo) used within expression X, if its death is in an instruction with luid between FROM_LUID (inclusive) and TO_INSN (exclusive), put a REG_DEAD note for that register in the list headed by PNOTES. gcc/combine.cc.signature: static bool reg_bitfield_target_p (rtx x, rtx body)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Return true if X is the target of a bit-field assignment in BODY, the pattern of an insn. X must be a REG.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void distribute_notes (rtx notes, rtx_insn *from_insn, rtx_insn *i3, rtx_insn *i2, rtx elim_i2, rtx elim_i1, rtx elim_i0)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Given a chain of REG_NOTES originally from FROM_INSN, try to place them as appropriate. gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void distribute_links (struct insn_link *links, rtx_insn *start, int limit)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Similarly to above, distribute the LOG_LINKS that used to be present on I3, I2, and I1 to new locations. gcc/combine.cc.signature: static bool unmentioned_reg_p (rtx equiv, rtx expr)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Check for any register or memory mentioned in EQUIV that is not mentioned in EXPR. This is used to restrict EQUIV to "specializations" of EXPR where some registers may have been replaced by constants.

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void make_more_copies (void)

gcc/combine.cc.signature: static void rest_of_handle_combine (void)
gcc/combine.cc.summary: Try combining insns through substitution.

reviewed_methods.summary: Helper function to do the actual work for expand_builtin_memset. The arguments to the builtin_memset call DEST, VAL, and LEN are broken out so that this can also be called without constructing an actual CALL_EXPR. The other arguments and return value are the same as for expand_builtin_memset.
reviewed_methods.reason: Primary dispatcher for inline memset expansion. It decides among store_by_pieces, set_storage_via_setmem, and related fallback paths based on size, alignment, and value form. The bug is exactly that builtin memset takes a scalar piecewise expansion path instead of an SSE-capable one, so this is the strongest fix point.

reviewed_methods.signature: static enum stringop_alg decide_alg (HOST_WIDE_INT count, HOST_WIDE_INT expected_size, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT min_size, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT max_size, bool memset, bool zero_memset, addr_space_t dst_as, addr_space_t src_as, int *dynamic_check, bool *noalign, bool recur)
reviewed_methods.summary: Given COUNT and EXPECTED_SIZE, decide on codegen of string operation.
reviewed_methods.reason: Most likely fix point. The bug is fundamentally a bad strategy choice for inline constant-size memset on x86: GCC chooses a scalar integer algorithm even though SSE unaligned vector stores are clearly legal and profitable for this exact 64-byte case. This function explicitly selects the stringop algorithm based on size, speed, and target costs, so it is the strongest candidate for steering memset toward an SSE-capable expansion path.

reviewed_methods.signature: static rtx emit_memset (rtx destmem, rtx destptr, rtx promoted_val, HOST_WIDE_INT size_to_move)
reviewed_methods.summary: This function emits moves to fill SIZE_TO_MOVE bytes starting from DESTMEM with value PROMOTED_VAL. SRC is passed by pointer to be updated on return. Return value is updated DST.
reviewed_methods.reason: Very strong candidate. After the memset path is chosen, this routine decides the move mode and emits the actual fill stores. The observed output of eight movq stores matches a piece-size/mode-selection issue here. If the fix is to allow/promote V16QI/TImode style stores for fixed-size fills with runtime byte values, this is a direct implementation point.

reviewed_methods.signature: bool ix86_expand_set_or_cpymem (rtx dst, rtx src, rtx count_exp, rtx val_exp, rtx align_exp, rtx expected_align_exp, rtx expected_size_exp, rtx min_size_exp, rtx max_size_exp, rtx probable_max_size_exp, bool issetmem)
reviewed_methods.summary: Expand string move (memcpy) ot store (memset) operation. Use i386 string operations when profitable. The code depends upon architecture, block size and alignment, but always has one of the following overall structures: Aligned move sequence: 1) Prologue guard: Conditional that jumps up to epilogues for small blocks that can be handled by epilogue alone. This is faster but also needed for correctness, since prologue assume the block is larger than the desired alignment. Optional dynamic check for size and libcall for large blocks is emitted here too, with -minline-stringops-dynamically. 2) Prologue: copy first few bytes in order to get destination aligned to DESIRED_ALIGN. It is emitted only when ALIGN is less than DESIRED_ALIGN and up to DESIRED_ALIGN - ALIGN bytes can be copied. We emit either a jump tree on power of two sized blocks, or a byte loop. 3) Main body: the copying loop itself, copying in SIZE_NEEDED chunks with specified algorithm. 4) Epilogue: code copying tail of the block that is too small to be handled by main body (or up to size guarded by prologue guard). Misaligned move sequence 1) missaligned move prologue/epilogue containing: a) Prologue handling small memory
reviewed_methods.reason: Central x86 string/memory expansion routine that decides algorithm, alignment handling, and profitability for memset lowering. Because the bug is x86-specific code-quality for inline constant-size memset under SSE4.2, this is one of the strongest backend-level fix locations.

reviewed_methods.signature: static fixed_size_mode widest_fixed_size_mode_for_size (unsigned int size, by_pieces_operation op)
reviewed_methods.summary: Return the widest mode that can be used to perform part of an operation OP on SIZE bytes. Try to use QI vector modes where possible.
reviewed_methods.reason: Highly suspicious because the symptom is exactly failure to choose a 16-byte vector mode for a 64-byte memset on an SSE target. This function explicitly selects the widest mode and mentions trying QI vector modes, making it one of the most likely places for a missed SSE opportunity.

reviewed_methods.signature: static rtx builtin_memset_gen_str (void *data, void *prev, HOST_WIDE_INT offset ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED, fixed_size_mode mode)
reviewed_methods.summary: Callback routine for store_by_pieces. Return the RTL of a register containing GET_MODE_SIZE (MODE) consecutive copies of the unsigned char value given in the RTL register data. For example, if mode is 4 bytes wide, return the RTL for 0x01010101*data. If PREV isn't nullptr, it has the RTL info from the previous iteration.
reviewed_methods.reason: Directly generates the repeated-byte value used by store_by_pieces and already contains separate VECTOR_MODE and scalar multiply-based broadcast logic. The observed bad codegen matches its scalar broadcast behavior closely, so if vector modes are available but not formed or preferred, this function is a very plausible local fix site.

reviewed_methods.signature: bool set_storage_via_setmem (rtx object, rtx size, rtx val, unsigned int align, unsigned int expected_align, HOST_WIDE_INT expected_size, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT min_size, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT max_size, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT probable_max_size)
reviewed_methods.summary: Expand a setmem pattern; return true if successful.
reviewed_methods.reason: This is the direct setmem-pattern expansion hook and a natural place for target-specific inline memset generation to succeed or fail. If x86 has a profitable SSE-capable setmem path that is not being selected for a 64-byte constant fill, this function is a strong candidate.

reviewed_methods.signature: rtx store_by_pieces (rtx to, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT len, by_pieces_constfn constfun, void *constfundata, unsigned int align, bool memsetp, memop_ret retmode)
reviewed_methods.summary: Generate several move instructions to store LEN bytes generated by CONSTFUN to block TO. (A MEM rtx with BLKmode). CONSTFUNDATA is a pointer which will be passed as argument in every CONSTFUN call. ALIGN is maximum alignment we can assume. MEMSETP is true if this is a memset operation and false if it's a copy of a constant string. Return value is based on RETMODE argument.
reviewed_methods.reason: Core driver for piecewise memset emission once that path is chosen. Since the bad assembly is eight separate stores, this infrastructure is clearly involved. Still, it is more likely the root issue is in earlier path/mode selection than in this thin wrapper itself.

reviewed_methods.signature: bool try_store_by_multiple_pieces (rtx to, rtx len, unsigned int ctz_len, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT min_len, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT max_len, rtx val, char valc, unsigned int align)
reviewed_methods.summary: Try to store VAL (or, if NULL_RTX, VALC) in LEN bytes starting at TO. Return TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise. TO is assumed to be aligned at an ALIGN-bits boundary. LEN must be a multiple of 1<<CTZ_LEN between MIN_LEN and MAX_LEN. The strategy is to issue one store_by_pieces for each power of two, from most to least significant, guarded by a test on whether there are at least that many bytes left to copy in LEN. ??? Should we skip some powers of two in favor of loops? Maybe start at the max of TO/LEN/word alignment, at least when optimizing for size, instead of ensuring O(log len) dynamic compares?
reviewed_methods.reason: Relevant when memset lowering uses multiple fixed-size stores, and it may influence store granularity. However, the reported failure looks more like the compiler chose the wrong overall memset expansion strategy before or outside this routine, so it is less likely than the main builtin expander or mode-selection code.

reviewed_methods.signature: bool imm_store_chain_info::output_merged_store (merged_store_group *group)
reviewed_methods.summary: Given a merged store group GROUP output the widened version of it. The store chain is against the base object BASE. Try store sizes of at most MAX_STORE_BITSIZE bits wide and don't output unaligned stores for STRICT_ALIGNMENT targets or if it's too expensive. Make sure that the number of statements output is less than the number of original statements. If a better sequence is possible emit it and return true.
reviewed_methods.reason: Moderately plausible because it controls widening and emission of merged stores, and the observed code does look like a widened scalar-store sequence. If memset is lowered into a store chain before final emission, this pass could cap width at 64-bit pieces instead of 128-bit vector stores. Still, the x86 stringop expander is a more direct and likely source.

reviewed_methods.signature: static unsigned int split_group (merged_store_group *group, bool allow_unaligned_store, bool allow_unaligned_load, bool bzero_first, vec<split_store *> *split_stores, unsigned *total_orig, unsigned *total_new)
reviewed_methods.summary: Split a merged store described by GROUP by populating the SPLIT_STORES vector (if non-NULL) with split_store structs describing the byte offset (from the base), the bit size and alignment of each store as well as the original statements involved in each such split group. This is to separate the splitting strategy from the statement building/emission/linking done in output_merged_store. Return number of new stores. If ALLOW_UNALIGNED_STORE is false, then all stores must be aligned. If ALLOW_UNALIGNED_LOAD is false, then all loads must be aligned. BZERO_FIRST may be true only when the first store covers the whole group and clears it; if BZERO_FIRST is true, keep that first store in the set unmodified and emit further stores for the overrides only. If SPLIT_STORES is NULL, it is just a dry run to count number of new stores.
reviewed_methods.reason: Possible contributor if store merging is fragmenting the 64-byte fill into 8-byte chunks based on alignment/profitability heuristics. But this seems secondary compared with x86-specific memset expansion logic, since the bug report is about constant-size memset codegen policy rather than general store-merging correctness.

reviewed_methods.signature: rtx expand_vector_broadcast (machine_mode vmode, rtx op)
reviewed_methods.summary: Create a new vector value in VMODE with all elements set to OP. The mode of OP must be the element mode of VMODE. If OP is a constant, then the return value will be a constant.
reviewed_methods.reason: Relevant conceptually because the missing optimization needs a byte splat into a vector register. However, the intrinsic case already proves GCC can form the broadcast when given vector-oriented IR. The problem seems more that memset expansion never chooses a vector path, not that generic vector broadcast formation itself is broken.

reviewed_methods.signature: static const char * ix86_get_ssemov (rtx *operands, unsigned size, enum attr_mode insn_mode, machine_mode mode)
reviewed_methods.summary: Return the opcode of the TYPE_SSEMOV instruction. To move from or to xmm16-xmm31/ymm16-ymm31 registers, we either require TARGET_AVX512VL or it is a register to register move which can be done with zmm register move.
reviewed_methods.reason: Also late in the pipeline and concerned with selecting the exact SSE move opcode given an already-formed SSE move. Since the compiler never seems to reach an SSE memset lowering path here, this is probably not the main fix location.

reviewed_methods.signature: const char * ix86_output_ssemov (rtx_insn *insn, rtx *operands)
reviewed_methods.summary: Return the template of the TYPE_SSEMOV instruction to move operands[1] into operands[0].
reviewed_methods.reason: This only prints the chosen SSE move instruction template once SSE moves are already selected. The reproducer shows GCC can emit movups fine for the intrinsic case, so the problem is unlikely to be in final asm formatting/output of SSE moves.

reviewed_methods.signature: bool maybe_legitimize_operands (enum insn_code icode, unsigned int opno, unsigned int nops, class expand_operand *ops)
reviewed_methods.summary: Try to make operands [OPS, OPS + NOPS) match operands [OPNO, OPNO + NOPS) of instruction ICODE. Return true on success, leaving the new operand values in the OPS themselves. Emit no code on failure.
reviewed_methods.reason: Too generic and one level removed. If operand legalization were the core bug, similar vector patterns would likely fail more broadly. Here the symptom is specifically a poorer memset lowering strategy, so this is unlikely to be the best fix location.

reviewed_methods.reason: Too indirect for this bug. The issue is a missed code-generation strategy for builtin memset, not obviously a combine legality rejection. Possible as a secondary blocker, but weak as the best fix location.
